doc.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021

title: Joy, Masekela's 'musician as doctor', and what aggravates him
summary: Joy for Turré is making people feel better; Masekela told him musicians are healers, and he describes dealing with unfocused bandmates.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Just to wrap up, is there anything that, on the bandstand or not on the bandstand, that makes you aggravated to the point of anger? And then I’ll flip that and what gives you great joy these days?

What gives me joy is making people happy, make them feel better. You know I was talking about playing with Hugh Masekela, I forgot to tell you why I brought that up. He told me, he said when he was a kid he used to, in high school he used to cut school and go play with the older guys at rehearsals and stuff. And they let him play, they saw a talented young man you can come on and play. But he was a kid so he was cutting up and being silly and stuff. And after a while they said, “Okay, calm down man, you’ve got to focus here man, you know?” “You know we can have fun but you have a responsibility too.” Of course he’s a kid, and you know how kids feel about the word “responsibility.” So he told me, he said, I said, “Well this is fun.” He said, “Yeah that’s cool but in our culture the musician is like a doctor. You’re supposed to make people feel good.” And you know that really went boing, that really rung a bell with me. So you know I always kind of felt that way but I didn’t realize it, you know when he said that it was oh, yeah. You know that’s one of the reasons, you know, that you do things. And a musician is another kind of healer you know, it’s not like giving you medicine or something like a pill, spiritual food. And also what I love about music, and especially jazz music, is it brings all people together from different cultures and races and what-have-you. It brings everybody together. And that’s what’s happening. All this divisiveness, yilch.

You know when I was younger if one of the musicians in the band was bullshitting and not really trying to do their best, it used to aggravate me, but I get older now I’ve learned that first of all it’s not worth the effort to let it upset you and take you off your track. either they’re going to get it or they’re not. And if it’s my band I just don’t call them anymore, but I thank them. But if it’s not my band I know I’m not going to be there, it’s not — I’m there to do the job and I go do the job and play the best that I can. But I’ve also been in bands where everybody is on a level with their focus and they’re trying with their whole essence — body, mind, and spirit — to do the absolute best that they can every time they take that horn out the case or sit at the piano or whatever. And you know that’s the environment I want to be in.
